To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tumor extracts from APO–AS have ACSA, BRA and B TGF activity.

extracts of canine apocrine celladenocarcinomaoftheanal sac (APO- AS) contain adenylate cyclasestimulating activity (ACS A) that is similar to synthetic bovine parathyroid hormone (b PTH) and that the ACS A is associated with bone-resorbing activi ty (B RA) and B transforming growth factor-like activity.
extracts of APO-AS contain potent, PTH-like ACSA, BRA, and a B TGF-like molecule which is co-purified with ACSA and is 10,000 fold more potent than the B TGF found in normal canine serum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of the ACSA from APO- AS.
the characterization and isolation of the bone-resorbing hormone from a canine apocrine cell anal sac tumor.
the characterization of a humoral bone-resorbing agent in APO- AS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ACSA is present in all APO-AS but is not present in normal anal sac or control tumors.
the humoral mediator responsible for hypercalcemia in APO- AS is PTHrP.
the tumor extracts contained a substance which stimulated adenylate cyclases, resorbed bone and had B TGF-like biological activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ACSA in canine APO-AS is a PTH-related protein, and that this protein also has bone-resorbing (B TGF-like) activity.
APO-AS contain a single mediator which has ACSA, BRA and B TGF activity.
the ACSA in APO- AS is due to a peptide with a sequence identical to or very similar to that of PTH, and that the ACSA and BRA are due to the same peptide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ACSA, BRA and B TGF found in APO- AS are all derived from the same molecular species.
ACSA, BRA and B TGF are present in extracts from APOAS, and that the ACSA in one extract was co-purified with B TGF.
the tumor extract from APO- AS contains a potent, PTH-like ACSA and BRA.
